items.slide_topic: GPT-6 Astra launch / largest training run

items.headline: An Interview with OpenAI President Greg Brockman About Astra and Alignment
items.dek: We're talking about the fact that this is the first run that we've trained on more than 100,000 GPUs, which is an easy number to throw around, but just think about the scale of that. These data centers in some ways are these big machines that we've built in order to help deliver and create AI technology...

items.headline: OpenAI and Oracle to deploy 450,000 GB200 GPUs at Stargate data center in Abilene, Texas
items.dek: Firms look set to occupy entire campus
items.author: Georgia Butler
items.caption: Cropped headline, dek, date and first two paragraphs incl. Ellison's '1.2GW ... one million four-bedroom homes' quote
items.notes: Body: 'The Stargate data center will use 1.2GW, "enough power for one million four-bedroom homes in the United States," the billionaire said.' Ellison added: 'That's a pretty good-sized city.' Power from 'a combination of grid energy and natural gas turbines'; eight buildings connected 'to support a single cluster'.

items.headline: SpaceX Form S-1 (filed May 20, 2026): COLOSSUS / COLOSSUS II compute power
items.dek: COLOSSUS and COLOSSUS II collectively provide approximately 1.0 gigawatt of compute power, with additional power capacity available for data center operations. ... At COLOSSUS II, we brought online the first cluster of approximately 110,000 GB200 processors, approximately 210 megawatts of compute power, even faster in 91 days.
items.caption: Screenshot of the S-1 paragraph (live sec.gov page)
items.notes: Also: 'the second cluster of 110,000 GB300 processors and 220 megawatts of compute power in 64 days'; next phase 'at least 220,000 additional GB300 processors and over 400 additional megawatts'; COLOSSUS: '~100,000 H100 processors, approximately 130 megawatts of compute power, in just 122 days'. Elsewhere: 'the first company to deploy a coherent gigawatt-scale AI training cluster' (company claim). SpaceX acquired xAI in Feb 2026. Key cross-check: 210 MW / 110,000 GB200 = 1.91 kW per GPU (IT, before cooling).

facts.claim: OpenAI: GPT-6 Astra was 'the first time we've pretrained on more than 100,000 GPUs at our Stargate site in Texas' - the company's largest training run 'by far' (Aidan Clark, VP of research).
Greg Brockman: 'this is the first run that we've trained on more than 100,000 GPUs, which is an easy number to throw around, but just think about the scale of that.'
Jensen Huang (via X): Astra was trained on '~100K+ Nvidia Grace Blackwell NVLink72'; plans to bring 400,000 GPUs online next (4x).
OpenAI's EU AI Act summary: GPT-6 Astra 'is not a modification or a fine-tune of a prior model' and was trained on 'More than 10 trillion tokens'; placed on the EU market 3 September 2026.
facts.source: OpenAI, Public Summary of Training Content for GPT-6 Astra (v1, 2 Sep 2026)

facts.claim: Epoch AI estimates GPT-6 Astra at ~1e27 FLOP (90% CI ~5e26-2e27) - 'corresponding to ~100k GB200s over 90 days at 25% FP8 MFU' - about 50x GPT-4 (~2.1e25), drawing ~233 MW (232.67 MW) during training.
facts.source: Epoch AI 'Data on AI models' (all_ai_models.csv, row last modified 2026-09-23)

facts.claim: Epoch's power method: Training power draw = PUE x Server overhead (1.82, from DGX H100: 10.2 kW / 8 x 700 W) x Power per GPU x Hardware quantity; PUE 1.08 in 2025, declining ~0.8%/yr. For Astra this implies ~1,200 W per GB200 x 1.82 x ~1.065 = ~2.33 kW per GPU all-in.

Stargate Abilene (Crusoe): 1.2 GW of power capacity; eight buildings; 'Each building has been designed to operate up to 50,000 NVIDIA GB200 NVL72s'; 206 MW coming online in 2025; design PUE 'an average of 1.2 to 1.3'.
Larry Ellison: Abilene will house more than 450,000 Nvidia GB200 GPUs and 'will use 1.2GW, "enough power for one million four-bedroom homes in the United States"' - 'That's a pretty good-sized city.'

Epoch AI: Abilene buildings 1-2 (100,800 GB200) were fully operational by Dec 24, 2025 at ~211 MW IT / ~295 MW total facility power; the site is now ~421 MW IT (509k H100e, $15.9B) and projected at 843 MW IT / ~1.18 GW facility by Nov 2026. Oracle posted on Apr 22, 2026: 'In Abilene, 200MW is already operational'.
facts.source: Epoch AI data center directory (updated Oct 2, 2026)

facts.claim: A GB200 NVL72 rack (72 GPUs + 36 Grace CPUs) has a TDP of 132 kW nominal (peak electrical design ~192 kW) - ~1.83 kW per GPU before cooling and cluster networking.

SpaceX S-1: at Colossus II, xAI brought online ~110,000 GB200 processors = ~210 MW of compute power in 91 days, then 110,000 GB300 = 220 MW in 64 days; next phase adds at least 220,000 GB300 and over 400 MW. Colossus + Colossus II provide ~1.0 GW of compute power.
Epoch AI: xAI's Colossus 2 (Memphis) runs ~946 MW of IT power (~1.28 GW incl. cooling), ~1.11M H100-equivalents, $35.8B; projected 1,531 MW IT by Q1 2027.

Zuckerberg: 'We're calling the first one Prometheus and it's coming online in '26. We're also building Hyperion, which will be able to scale up to 5GW over several years.' Epoch now estimates Prometheus at 471 MW IT (~612 MW facility, Aug 2026); Hyperion's first phase ~1.6 GW IT (~2.2 GW facility) by 2028.

Anthropic: deal with Amazon for 'up to 5 gigawatts (GW) of capacity for training and deploying Claude' with 'nearly 1GW total of Trainium2 and Trainium3 capacity coming online by the end of 2026'; 'we currently use over one million Trainium2 chips'. Epoch: the Anthropic-Amazon New Carlisle (Project Rainier) campus is at ~910 MW IT (~1.09 GW facility).

Epoch AI/EPRI: power for the largest training runs has grown ~2.2x per year; 'the largest individual frontier training runs in 2030 will likely draw 4-16 gigawatts (GW) of power, or enough to power millions of US homes.'
Epoch AI: '>100 GW of total AI capacity worldwide and >50 GW in the US is plausible by 2030, which would approach 5% of the US's total power generation capacity.'
New York City (NYISO Zone J) used 50,104 GWh of electricity in 2025 (49,703 GWh in 2024) - an average load of ~5.7 GW, ~137 GWh per day, ~961 GWh per week; its 2025 summer peak was 10,825 MW.
facts.source: NYISO 2026 Gold Book, Tables I-2 & I-4a; Zone J = New York City per NYISO Power Trends 2026

facts.claim: The average US residential electricity customer used 863 kWh per month in 2024 (~10,360 kWh/yr); EIA's FAQ gives 10,791 kWh for 2022.
facts.source: EIA Electric Sales, Revenue, and Average Price, Table 5A (2024); EIA FAQ

facts.claim: DOE: 'A typical nuclear reactor produces 1 gigawatt of power per plant on average.'
facts.source: U.S. DOE Office of Nuclear Energy

facts.claim: Hoover Dam: nameplate capacity 'about 2,080 megawatts'; average annual net generation 1947-2008 'about 4.2 billion kilowatt-hours' (~480 MW average output).
facts.source: U.S. Bureau of Reclamation, Hoover Dam FAQ

facts.claim: ARITHMETIC (claim check): 100,000 GPUs x ~2.33 kW all-in (Epoch) = ~233 MW; x 90 days x 24 h = ~503 GWh. NYC uses 50,104 GWh / 365 x 7 = ~961 GWh per week. So Astra's pretraining ~ 0.52 of a NYC-week = ~3.7 days of New York City's electricity - roughly HALF the 'NYC for a week' claim. Range: 2.2 days (206 MW, 60 days) to 6.1 days (293 MW peak facility power, 120 days). Matching a full week at 233 MW would need ~172 days of pretraining.
facts.source: Inputs: Epoch AI, Crusoe, NYISO (our arithmetic)

facts.claim: At ~233 MW, the Astra training cluster drew ~4% of NYC's average load (~2% of its 2025 peak) - the continuous use of ~197,000 average US homes, about a quarter of a typical nuclear reactor, or half of Hoover Dam's average output. The ~503 GWh run equals a year of electricity for ~48,500 US homes.
facts.source: Derived from Epoch AI, NYISO, EIA, DOE, USBR

facts.claim: Measured in New York City's electricity: training GPT-3 (2020) ~ 18 minutes; GPT-4 (2023) ~ 8 hours; Grok 3 (2025) ~ 1.7 days; GPT-6 Astra (2026) ~ 3.7 days (Epoch estimates of power x duration).
facts.source: Derived from Epoch AI model DB + NYISO

facts.claim: The next step Huang describes - 400,000 GPUs - at the same ~2.33 kW per GPU would draw ~0.93 GW: one nuclear reactor, ~16% of NYC's average load. Epoch's 2030 forecast for one training run (4-16 GW) spans 0.7x to 2.8x NYC's average load - the top end is ~1.5x NYC's 2025 summer peak (10.8 GW).
facts.source: Derived from PC Gamer/Huang, Epoch AI, NYISO

arithmetic.question: Did training GPT-6 (Astra) on ~100k GPUs use about as much electricity as New York City uses in a week?

gpu_count.note: 'more than 100,000 GPUs' (OpenAI via Fortune; Brockman via Stratechery); GB200 NVL72 per Huang; Abilene bldg 1-2 = 100,800 GB200 (Epoch citing Crusoe)

kw_per_gpu_all_in.note: low = Crusoe 206 MW / 100,000; central = Epoch 232.67 MW / 100,000 (1,200 W x 1.82 x PUE ~1.065); high = Epoch peak facility 295 MW / 100,800. All assume near-peak draw; real average draw is likely lower.

training_days.note: Undisclosed. 90 days = Epoch's assumption; Epoch notes many frontier runs now exceed 100 days.

arithmetic.formula: energy_GWh = gpus x kW_per_gpu x days x 24 / 1e6 ; nyc_weeks = energy_GWh / (50,104 x 7 / 365)
arithmetic.verdict: Overstated by ~2x. Central estimate ~503 GWh = ~3.7 days (~0.52 week) of NYC electricity; plausible range ~2-6 days. Reaching a full NYC-week would need ~172 days of pretraining at ~233 MW, or ~137 days even at Epoch's peak facility power (~293 MW) - longer than any evidence suggests. Safe slide phrasing: 'Training GPT-6 Astra used roughly as much electricity as New York City uses in 3-4 days (Epoch-based estimate).'
